# Lixity

> Lixity is a deterministic, offline text-linguistics engine for literary
> manuscripts: sentence rhythm, length-invariant lexical diversity, readability,
> register signals, paragraph-accurate tense profiles, and a self-calibrating
> style reference (median/MAD bands, significance-adjusted z*, Benjamini-Hochberg
> FDR). It never judges style against external norms. Pure Python, 7 languages
> (de, en, fr, es, it, pt, nl) plus a generic fallback, no cloud, byte-identical
> output for identical input.

License: Lixity Non-Commercial License 1.0 (LNCL-1.0) – source-available, not
open source; free for research, education, personal writing and non-commercial
open science; commercial use requires a written license
(mfahsold@googlemail.com). Full text:
https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/LICENSE

## Primary documentation

- [README](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity#readme): overview, install, CLI quick start, capabilities, license
- [docs/USAGE.md](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md): full command reference, worked example, metrics, known limitations
- [docs/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md): JSON contracts, interpretation heuristics, stable Python facade, dashboard DOM hooks
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history (current: 1.8.0)

Reports/CLI messages: English default, German via LIXITY_LANG=de. JSON contracts:
schema_version 2 (analyze/profile, language-neutral tense values
present/past/mixed/neutral) and 2 (style reference).

## Commands (all offline, deterministic, UTF-8)

- `lixity analyze FILE --json` – corpus metrics + per-chapter style features (schema v1)
- `lixity profile FILE` – paragraph-accurate tense/style profiles
- `lixity dialogue FILE [--json]` – dialogue turn structure (turns, turn lengths, per chapter)
- `lixity characters FILE --names A,B [--json]` – character presence per chapter (aliases supported)
- `lixity style FILE --json` – self-calibrating style reference (schema v2)
- `lixity dashboard FILE -o ui.html` – single-file interactive HTML dashboard (clickable KPIs, status strip, deviation layer, work markers)
- `lixity build [FILE] [--dry-run]` – idempotent workspace build into `exports/` (zero writes for unchanged input)
- `lixity about --json` – languages, features, heuristics
- `lixity completion bash|zsh` – shell completion

Python facade: `from lixity import api` – `analyze`, `profile`,
`fingerprint`/`passport`, `dashboard`, `markers`/`add_marker`/`resolve_marker`,
`about`.

## Key numbers and thresholds

- z* = (x − median) / sqrt(sigma^2 + SE^2), sigma = 1.4826 * MAD; |z*| >= 2.5 noticeable, >= 3.5 strong
- FDR control: Benjamini-Hochberg, q = 0.05
- Lexical diversity guards: MTLD and Maas a2 need >= 100 tokens, HD-D >= 175 tokens, MATTR >= 50-token window
- Style reference needs several chapters with measurable spread

## Project

- Source: https://github.com/mfahsold/lixity
- Project page: https://mfahsold.github.io/lixity/
- Sample corpus: two public-domain works – *Effi Briest* (Fontane, 1895, Project Gutenberg #5323)
  and *Pride and Prejudice* (Austen, 1813, #1342); unmodified PG source files plus Markdown
  conversions, not relicensed by the LNCL
- Third-party: pydantic (MIT), rich (MIT), orjson (MIT/Apache-2.0)
